topic: Classification of errors and suspense account
question: Explain the different types of errors that may occur in the books of account. Which of them affect the agreement of the trial balance, and when is a suspense account opened?
sources: Standard accounting principles: rectification of errors and the trial balance (ICAI Foundation syllabus, accounting process)

points.label: Errors of principle
points.description: An entry made against a basic accounting principle, such as treating capital expenditure as revenue expenditure or the other way round (for example, cost of machinery debited to purchases account).
points.basis: Accounting principle: classification of errors - errors of principle

points.label: Errors of omission
points.description: A transaction is left out of the books wholly (complete omission) or partly (partial omission, such as recorded in the journal but not posted to the ledger).
points.basis: Accounting principle: classification of errors - errors of omission

points.label: Errors of commission
points.description: Wrong recording such as wrong amount, wrong casting (totalling), wrong carrying forward, wrong side or wrong account posting.
points.basis: Accounting principle: classification of errors - errors of commission

points.label: Compensating errors
points.description: Two or more errors whose effects cancel out each other, so the trial balance still agrees.
points.basis: Accounting principle: classification of errors - compensating errors

points.label: Effect on trial balance and suspense account
points.description: Complete omission, errors of principle, compensating errors and posting to the wrong account on the correct side do not disturb the trial balance; one-sided errors (wrong totals, partial postings, wrong side) do. If the trial balance does not agree and the error cannot be found at once, the difference is put in a suspense account, which is closed when the errors are rectified.
points.basis: Accounting principle: trial balance and use of a suspense account in rectification of errors
